name: Smack Apparel
old_description: Since 1998, we’ve been making bold, unlicensed, and unapologetic gear that turns heads, starts conversations, and pisses off rival fans—in the best way possible.
about:
Smack Apparel was founded in 1998 in Tampa, Florida, by sports enthusiasts who wanted to create bold, unlicensed fan gear that sparks conversation at tailgates. The company operates its own screen-printing facility in Tampa, where it designs and produces all of its apparel.

The product line spans adult t-shirts (short and long sleeve), baby onesies, and toddler gear covering college football, professional football, and professional baseball. A separate Bushwood Prints collection offers fine art prints and tumblers featuring artwork by David O'Keefe. All garments use 100% cotton, 6 oz preshrunk fabric and are printed in-house; sizes range from small to 5XL.

Smack Apparel sells directly to end consumers via its website, targeting fans of specific programs such as Notre Dame, Michigan, Florida State, and professional teams like Chicago football. The company also serves parents and gift buyers with its Rookie Wear infant and toddler line. Products are explicitly unlicensed, with the company stating they are "licensed only by the 1st Amendment."

The brand differentiates itself through domestic production, original designs that lean into rivalry humor, and a fan-first voice that avoids corporate licensing restrictions.
